title: The Best Yearbook
premise: Xanthe Vasquez transfers to Hollow Creek High, a school built over the flooded ruins of the town's first settlement, determined to stay invisible until graduation. But an anonymous group chat called 'The Best Yearbook' begins posting predictions of the future — small at first, then deadly — and every member is a student the school has already forgotten. Xanthe realizes the chat is fed by something beneath the gymnasium that trades foresight for memory: to know what's coming, you must be erased from the record. To save the classmates marked for erasure, Xanthe must enter and win the state championship that everyone watches — and the older, stranger contest running underneath it — sacrificing their own place in the yearbook, and in memory, so the others survive. In the end, one photo remains that no one can explain: a stranger smiling in the back row, whom everyone feels they almost remember.
about_author: Ada Pemberton grew up in a river town where the high school sat on pilings above the old flood line, and she never stopped wondering what was down there. She writes young adult fiction about kids who survive things adults prefer to forget.

chapters.title: Enrollment
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Arriving mid-year at Hollow Creek High, Xanthe catalogs exits, cliques, and rules for invisibility, noting the school's odd architecture — hallways that dead-end into the 1962 wing. Emotional beat: guarded relief; a fresh start is possible if no one looks too closely.

chapters.title: The Flood Line
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. In history class, a teacher mentions the original town drowned under the reservoir, and the school was built on its bones. Xanthe feels watched in the basement locker rooms. Beat: unease planted beneath the routine of new-kid survival.

chapters.title: Group Chat: Unknown Number
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. A group chat invites Xanthe by name — though no one gave out their number. Six other students are in it, all quiet kids from the margins. The first prediction posts: a fire drill at 10:14 tomorrow. It happens exactly. Beat: fascinated dread.

chapters.title: The Others
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Xanthe meets the chat members: Marisol, who predicts weather; Dev, who knows test answers before they're written; quiet Theo; twins Priya and Sam; and Juniper, who claims she joined last year and can't remember her old friends. Beat: belonging, tentatively, for the first time.

chapters.title: Rules of the Game
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. She explains the pattern: predictions come true, then the predictor loses a memory — a face, a name, a whole friendship. The chat calls it 'paying tuition.' Xanthe refuses to believe until Dev forgets his own brother's birthday mid-sentence. Beat: horror arriving through small losses.

chapters.title: Homecoming, Predicted
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The chat predicts a tragedy at homecoming — bleachers, 9:41 PM. They debate warning people and risk exposure, or letting it happen. Xanthe argues for intervention; the group splits. Beat: first moral fracture inside the fragile found family.

Xanthe's POV. They trigger a false alarm and clear the bleachers; the section collapses empty. No one dies — but the chat goes silent for three days, and when it returns, its tone has changed, colder, addressing them as 'contestants.' Beat: victory curdling into being played.

chapters.title: What the Gym Is Built On
chapters.summary: Theo's POV. Theo and Xanthe find blueprints in the archive: the gymnasium sits directly over the drowned town square, and the 1962 wing matches no approved plan. Old yearbooks show students photographed in the same seats across decades — identical faces. Beat: the scale of the mystery widens.

chapters.title: Tuition Due
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya wakes unable to remember Sam — her own twin walks past her like a stranger. The group realizes the entity takes memories as payment whether or not they use their gifts. Beat: grief and guilt; knowledge has a price none of them agreed to.

chapters.title: The Championship That Doesn't Matter
chapters.summary: Dev's POV. A prediction names the state swim finals — and Xanthe, a former competitive swimmer, as a qualifier. The chat frames it as 'Round One.' Xanthe, who quit swimming after a scandal at their old school, must rejoin the team and be visible again. Beat: terror of exposure versus duty.

chapters.title: Visible
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Tryouts go badly; teammates dig up rumors from Xanthe's past. Marisol defends them publicly, and Xanthe experiences real friendship in daylight for the first time. Beat: warmth earned at the cost of the invisibility Xanthe thought they wanted.

chapters.title: The 1962 Wing
chapters.summary: Juniper's POV. Following a prediction, the five enter the sealed wing at night and find classrooms frozen mid-lesson, attendance sheets with their own names dated decades ago. Juniper finds her own photo from 1987. Beat: vertigo — they were chosen long before they arrived.

chapters.title: Contestants
chapters.summary: Sam's POV. The chat finally explains itself: the thing below runs a contest every generation. Winners keep their futures; losers become 'yearbook entries' — remembered by no one, folded into the record. The championship is Round Two. Beat: stakes made explicit and unbearable.

chapters.title: Everyone Forgets Juniper
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs, fragmenting. Overnight, Juniper is erased — teachers skip her desk, her mother doesn't answer, only the four remaining contestants remember. They find her waiting in the 1962 wing, half-faded, still joking. Beat: devastating proof the threat is real and immediate.

chapters.title: The Deal Nobody Signed
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Researching the drowned town, Xanthe learns the original bargain: in 1962 the town traded its children's futures to the water to survive the flood. The contest is the debt renewing itself. There may be a loophole — a champion can pay for everyone. Beat: grim hope with a terrible price tag.

chapters.title: Heats
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Sectionals: Xanthe swims angry and fast, qualifying for state while the group runs interference against the entity's distractions — hallucinations in the water, missing gear, tampered times. Beat: determination forged; Xanthe chooses to fight instead of hide.

chapters.title: What We'd Forget
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. The group makes contingency plans: letters, recordings, a shared document of everything they refuse to lose. Each writes what they'd want remembered if erased. Quiet confessions surface — why each of them needed to be invisible. Beat: tender, aching intimacy before the endgame.

chapters.title: State Finals
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. The championship that everyone watches. Xanthe swims the race of their life in front of the whole school — and wins, but the crowd's cheers sound wrong, layered, like applause from underwater. The pool drains itself between events. Round Three is beginning. Beat: triumph shadowed by dread.

chapters.title: Below
chapters.summary: All six POVs interwoven. The finalists descend through the drained pool into the flooded square, where the contest's true form waits: a mirror-water arena showing each contestant the life they'd keep if the others paid. It offers Xanthe everything — a past without scandal, a future with friends intact — if only the others are entered. Beat: temptation at maximum pressure.

chapters.title: The Best Yearbook
chapters.summary: Xanthe's POV. Climax. Xanthe refuses the trade and instead claims the champion's right: to substitute themselves for all entries. The entity accepts — one name for six. Xanthe signs the yearbook page with their own hand and lets the water take their record. Beat: sacrificial courage; the invisible kid becomes the price.

chapters.title: Attendance
chapters.summary: Marisol's POV. Aftermath: the 1962 wing crumbles, the chat dissolves, Juniper returns to her life. The five wake to a school where no one remembers Xanthe Vasquez — except each other, because they wrote it all down. They hold a private memorial with the recordings. Beat: grief braided with gratitude.

chapters.title: Back Row, Smiling
chapters.summary: Final chapter, rotating close-third among the five, ending on Marisol. Graduation. The new yearbook arrives; in the candid of the state finals crowd, a stranger smiles in the back row, and all five feel they almost know the face. Marisol writes the name 'Xanthe' in the margin anyway. Beat: bittersweet resolution — memory kept alive by choice, not magic.
